newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Airlines issues jet fuel term tender.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Airlines issues jet fuel term tender.

text.p: Singapore Airlines (SIA) has issued a term tender on Wednesday to buy aviation jet fuel for one or two year deliveries worldwide, an industry source said.
For the first time SIA amended the contract pricing formula for cargoes to be lifted from locations which use Singapore benchmark prices, the source said.

The change allowed suppliers the option to offer cargoes based either on 50 percent of the Platt's published price assessments in Singapore and 50 percent on the Far East Oil Pricing (FEOP) quotations, or 100 percent Platt's.
But products lifted from locations that are priced off the U.S. and European benchmark remained unchanged at 100 percent Platt's, he said.
The tender seeks the deliveries of cargoes from 37 locations worldwide involving 380 million U.S. gallons (15.9 million barrels) of jet fuel, the source said.
SIA's annual jet fuel requirements are estimated at 950 million U.S. gallons or 22.62 million barrels.
The tender requests for physical deliveries during fiscal 1997-1998 (April 1-March 31) for one-year contracts and during fiscal 1997-1999 for two year contracts.
Companies have the option to offer one-or-two-year supply contracts, the source said.
The tender closes on December 10 and offers will be valid until March 1997, he said.
SIA would be the second Asian airlines to use the FEOP pricing assessment in its jet fuel purchases if it awarded the latest tender using the 50-50 formula based on Platt's and FEOP.
Japan Airlines was the first regional airlines to use the FEOP formula.
In response to Reuters queries in September, a JAL official said they attributed part of the current high prices to the structural problem of Asia's pricing mechanism.
"When many airlines and oil companies use FEOP, we will have more stable prices, if not necessarily lower," the official said.
